title: 4058. Maximum Pulse Value After One Subarray Rotation

examples.explanation: The original pulse value is 1 - 5 + 2 = -2. Rotate the subarray nums[0..1] from [1, 5] to [5, 1]. The resulting array is [5, 1, 2] and its pulse value is 5 - 1 + 2 = 6, which is the maximum possible.
The original pulse value is 6 - 4 + 3 = 5. Rotate the subarray nums[1..2] from [4, 3] to [3, 4]. The resulting array is [6, 3, 4] and its pulse value is 6 - 3 + 4 = 7, which is the maximum possible.
The original pulse value is 9 - 7 = 2, which is already maximum. Thus, no rotation is required.

hints: After rotating nums[l..r], every element originally at an index from l + 1 through r changes its contribution's sign. The element nums[l] moves to index r.
Let P[t] be the alternating sum of the first t elements, with P[0] = 0. The change in pulse value is 2 * (P[l + 1] - P[r + 1]) when l and r have the same parity, and 2 * (P[l] - P[r + 1]) otherwise.

Scan r from left to right. Among indices l < r, maintain the maximum values of P[l] and P[l + 1] separately for each parity of l. Use these maxima to find the best gain in constant time per index, allowing a gain of zero for skipping the operation.
